reason: The latest month in which at least 43 of the 47 counties have a risk index. The very newest month is often still arriving, so it may be skipped.
sql: SELECT MAX(month) AS latest_complete_month FROM (SELECT month FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(risk_index) >= 43) AS m LIMIT 500

reason: Counts counties with a risk index above 0.5 in the latest month that has a risk index for at least 43 of 47 counties. The month is shown so you can see which one was used.
sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT month FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(risk_index) >= 43 ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT r.month, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE r.risk_index > 0.5) AS counties_drier_or_browner_than_usual FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly AS r JOIN latest USING (month) GROUP BY r.month LIMIT 500

reason: Turkana's share of people in IPC Phase 3 or worse in its latest analysis, as a fraction (0.25 = 25%). If Turkana was assessed in several areas the figure combines them; check is_partial_county if coverage matters.
sql: SELECT analysis_month, share_phase3plus FROM marts.fct_ipc_county_analysis WHERE county_name = 'Turkana' ORDER BY analysis_month DESC LIMIT 1

reason: Lists counties whose risk index was above 0.5 (drier or browner than usual) in all of the 3 latest months with data for at least 43 of 47 counties. Each county is compared with its own history, so this shows unusual conditions, not which counties are worst off.
sql: WITH months AS (SELECT month FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(risk_index) >= 43 ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 3) SELECT r.county_name FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly AS r JOIN months USING (month) GROUP BY r.county_name HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE r.risk_index > 0.5) = 3 ORDER BY r.county_name LIMIT 500

reason: The latest published 3-month maize price forecast for each of the 16 FEWS NET counties with its 80% range, sorted from the largest expected rise to the largest fall (change_pct is the percent change from the latest price). Garissa's prices are reported in coarse steps, so its forecast is less reliable.
sql: SELECT county_name, target_month, forecast_kes_per_kg, lower_80_kes_per_kg, upper_80_kes_per_kg, change_pct FROM marts.fct_price_forecast WHERE horizon = 3 ORDER BY change_pct DESC LIMIT 500

reason: The 5 counties with the highest share of people in IPC Phase 3 or worse in the latest IPC analysis (a fraction; 0.25 = 25%). Only counties IPC assessed are included, and some may cover only part of the county.
sql: SELECT county_name, share_phase3plus FROM marts.fct_ipc_county_analysis WHERE analysis_month = (SELECT MAX(analysis_month) FROM marts.fct_ipc_county_analysis) ORDER BY share_phase3plus DESC LIMIT 5

reason: Shows the month since January 2015 with the most counties at a risk index of 0.8 or more (strongly unusual), taking the most recent month if tied. The newest month may be incomplete, which could only lower its count.
sql: SELECT month, COUNT(*) AS counties_strongly_unusual FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly WHERE month >= CAST('2015-01-01' AS DATE) AND risk_index >= 0.8 GROUP BY month ORDER BY counties_strongly_unusual DESC, month DESC LIMIT 1

reason: Counties ranked by their average risk index over the 12 latest months with data for at least 43 of 47 counties, highest (drier or browner than usual) first. Each county is compared only with its own history, so this ranks recent rainfall and vegetation shocks, not how food insecure a county is.
sql: WITH months AS (SELECT month FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(risk_index) >= 43 ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 12) SELECT r.county_name, AVG(r.risk_index) AS avg_risk_index FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly AS r JOIN months USING (month) WHERE r.risk_index IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.county_name ORDER BY avg_risk_index DESC LIMIT 500

reason: Shows the 3 counties with the highest risk index (driest/browniest compared with their own history) in each of the 3 latest months with data for at least 43 counties. This does not show which counties are most food insecure, since the index only compares each county with its own past.
sql: WITH months AS (SELECT month FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(risk_index) >= 43 ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 3), ranked AS (SELECT r.month, r.county_name, r.risk_index, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.month ORDER BY r.risk_index DESC, r.county_name) AS rn FROM marts.fct_risk_index_monthly AS r JOIN months USING (month) WHERE r.risk_index IS NOT NULL) SELECT month, county_name, risk_index FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY month DESC, risk_index DESC, county_name LIMIT 500

reason: Counties where the Phase 3+ share was at least 0.20 in 3 or more IPC analyses, with the number of such analyses. Only counties IPC assessed appear, and partial-county areas are included, so some shares may cover only part of a county.
sql: SELECT county_name, COUNT(*) AS analyses_with_20pct_or_more FROM marts.fct_ipc_county_analysis WHERE share_phase3plus >= 0.2 GROUP BY county_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY analyses_with_20pct_or_more DESC, county_name LIMIT 500
